\chapter{Chapter03 — Estimation}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from FABL.Chapter03.GoldreichLevinAlgorithm.Estimation
\section{Overview}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{FABL.Chapter03.GoldreichLevinAlgorithm.Estimation}.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Goldreich–Levin weight accuracy]
\lean{FABL.goldreichLevinWeightAccuracy}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p084-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p084-b005,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p085-b002
}
\label{FABL.goldreichLevinWeightAccuracy}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.GoldreichLevinThreshold, FABL.PositiveLearningParameter}
For a threshold $\tau\in(0,1]$, the Goldreich–Levin weight accuracy parameter is
$\tau^2/4$, viewed as a rational in $(0,1/2]$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Goldreich–Levin call confidence]
\lean{FABL.goldreichLevinCallConfidence}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p085-b004}
\label{FABL.goldreichLevinCallConfidence}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.GoldreichLevinThreshold, FABL.PositiveLearningParameter, FABL.goldreichLevinActiveCap}
For a natural number $n$ and threshold $\tau\in(0,1]$, the call confidence parameter is
$1/[40(n+1)(A(\tau)+1)]$, where $A(\tau)$ is the active cap at threshold $\tau$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Goldreich–Levin estimate record]
\lean{FABL.GoldreichLevinEstimateRecord}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p084-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p084-b005
}
\label{FABL.GoldreichLevinEstimateRecord}
\leanok
For $n\in\mathbb N$, an estimate record consists of a finite set of coordinates in
$\mathrm{Fin}(n)$, a finite frequency prefix in $\mathrm{Fin}(n)$, and a rational
estimate.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Estimate record key]
\lean{FABL.GoldreichLevinEstimateRecord.key}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p084-b002}
\label{FABL.GoldreichLevinEstimateRecord.key}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.GoldreichLevinEstimateRecord}
For $n\in\mathbb N$, the key of an estimate record is the ordered pair consisting of its
coordinate set and its frequency prefix.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Matching estimate record]
\lean{FABL.GoldreichLevinEstimateRecord.Matches}
\label{FABL.GoldreichLevinEstimateRecord.Matches}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.GoldreichLevinEstimateRecord}
Let $n$ be a natural number, and let a record contain a coordinate set, a frequency
prefix, and a rational estimate. The record matches a given coordinate set $J$ and
frequency prefix if its stored coordinate set equals $J$ and its stored frequency prefix
equals that prefix.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Accuracy of an estimate record]
\lean{FABL.GoldreichLevinEstimateRecord.IsAccurate}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p085-b002}
\label{FABL.GoldreichLevinEstimateRecord.IsAccurate}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.GoldreichLevinEstimateRecord, FABL.GoldreichLevinThreshold, FABL.freeFrequencyPart, FABL.restrictedFourierWeight}
Let $n\in\mathbb N$, let a record contain a coordinate set and frequency prefix, let
$f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\{−1,1\}$ be a Boolean function, and let $\tau\in(0,1]$. The record is
accurate for $f$ at threshold $\tau$ when the absolute difference between its rational
estimate and the restricted Fourier weight of $f$ on its coordinate set at the free part
of its frequency prefix is less than $\tau^2/4$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Estimate recovered from a trace]
\lean{FABL.goldreichLevinTraceEstimate}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p084-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p084-b005
}
\label{FABL.goldreichLevinTraceEstimate}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.GoldreichLevinEstimateRecord, FABL.GoldreichLevinEstimateRecord.Matches, FABL.RestrictedFourierWeightEstimate, FABL.liftFreeFrequency}
For $n\in\mathbb N$, a trace of estimate records defines a restricted Fourier weight
estimate as follows: for a coordinate set $J$ and a frequency set $S\subseteq J$, use
the estimate from the first record in the trace whose coordinate set is $J$ and whose
frequency prefix is the lift of $S$; if there is no such record, use zero.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Accuracy of an estimate trace]
\lean{FABL.GoldreichLevinEstimateTrace.IsAccurate}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p084-b005}
\label{FABL.GoldreichLevinEstimateTrace.IsAccurate}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.GoldreichLevinEstimateRecord, FABL.GoldreichLevinEstimateRecord.IsAccurate, FABL.GoldreichLevinThreshold}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\tau\in\mathbb{Q}$ satisfy $0<\tau\leq 1$, let
$f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$ be a Boolean function, and let a trace be a finite list of
estimate records. The trace is accurate for $f$ at threshold $\tau$ if every record in
it has estimate differing from the restricted Fourier weight of $f$ on its recorded
coordinate set and frequency prefix by less than $\tau^2/4$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Coverage of frequency prefixes]
\lean{FABL.GoldreichLevinEstimateTrace.Covers}
\label{FABL.GoldreichLevinEstimateTrace.Covers}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.GoldreichLevinEstimateRecord, FABL.GoldreichLevinEstimateRecord.Matches}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let a trace be a finite list of estimate records, let $J$
be a subset of the $n$ coordinates, and let $frequencies$ be a finite family of
subsets of those coordinates. The trace covers this family at $J$ if, for every member
of the family, it contains a record whose coordinate set is $J$ and whose frequency
prefix is that member.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Accuracy of a Covered Trace Estimate]
\lean{FABL.goldreichLevinTraceEstimate_accurate_of_mem}
\label{FABL.goldreichLevinTraceEstimate_accurate_of_mem}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.GoldreichLevinEstimateRecord, FABL.GoldreichLevinEstimateRecord.IsAccurate, FABL.GoldreichLevinEstimateRecord.Matches, FABL.GoldreichLevinEstimateTrace.Covers, FABL.GoldreichLevinEstimateTrace.IsAccurate, FABL.GoldreichLevinThreshold, FABL.freeFrequencyPart, FABL.goldreichLevinTraceEstimate, FABL.liftFreeFrequency_freeFrequencyPart_eq_of_subset, FABL.restrictedFourierWeight}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $0<\\tau\\le1$, and let $f$ map the
$n$-dimensional sign cube to signs. Suppose every record in a finite trace has estimate
within strictly less than $\\tau^2/4$ of its corresponding restricted Fourier weight.
Let $J$ be a set of coordinates, let $F$ be a finite family of coordinate subsets
covered by the trace (each $U\\in F$ has a record with coordinate set $J$ and frequency
prefix $U$), and take $U\\in F$ with $U\\subseteq J$. The trace estimate at $J$ and the
free part of $U$ differs from the restricted Fourier weight of $f$ at that same
coordinate set and free part by strictly less than $\\tau^2/4$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Candidate estimate program]
\lean{FABL.goldreichLevinCandidateEstimateProgram}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p083-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p085-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p085-b004
}
\label{FABL.goldreichLevinCandidateEstimateProgram}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.GoldreichLevinEstimateRecord, FABL.GoldreichLevinThreshold, FABL.LearningProgram, FABL.LearningProgram.map, FABL.freeFrequencyPart, FABL.goldreichLevinCallConfidence, FABL.goldreichLevinWeightAccuracy, FABL.scheduledRestrictedFourierWeightEstimatorProgram}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\tau\in\mathbb{Q}$ satisfy $0<\tau\leq 1$, and let $J$
and $P$ be sets of coordinates in $\{1,\ldots,n\}$. The candidate estimate program uses
membership queries to run the scheduled restricted Fourier-weight estimator for $J$ and
the part of $P$ lying in $J$, with the accuracy and confidence parameters specified by
$\tau$ and $n$, then returns an estimate record containing $J$, $P$, and the resulting
rational estimate.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Candidate estimate record key]
\lean{FABL.goldreichLevinCandidateEstimateProgram_key}
\label{FABL.goldreichLevinCandidateEstimateProgram_key}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.GoldreichLevinEstimateRecord, FABL.GoldreichLevinEstimateRecord.key, FABL.GoldreichLevinThreshold, FABL.LearningCost, FABL.LearningProgram.runWithCost, FABL.LearningProgram.runWithCost_map, FABL.goldreichLevinCandidateEstimateProgram}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\{−1,1\}$ be any target function, let
$0<\tau\le 1$ be a rational threshold, and let $J$ and $P$ be subsets of the $n$
coordinates. Every outcome in the support of the candidate-estimation program run with
inputs $\tau,J,P$ has an estimate record whose coordinate set is $J$ and whose frequency
prefix is $P$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Candidate estimator query count]
\lean{FABL.goldreichLevinCandidateEstimateProgram_queries_eq}
\label{FABL.goldreichLevinCandidateEstimateProgram_queries_eq}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.GoldreichLevinEstimateRecord, FABL.GoldreichLevinThreshold, FABL.LearningCost, FABL.LearningProgram.runWithCost, FABL.LearningProgram.runWithCost_map, FABL.fourierEstimatorSampleCount, FABL.freeFrequencyPart, FABL.goldreichLevinCallConfidence, FABL.goldreichLevinCandidateEstimateProgram, FABL.goldreichLevinWeightAccuracy, FABL.scheduledRestrictedFourierWeightEstimatorProgram_queries_eq}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\{−1,1\}$ be any target function, let
$0<\tau\le 1$ be a rational threshold, and let $J$ and $P$ be subsets of the $n$
coordinates. Every outcome in the support of the candidate-estimation program run with
inputs $\tau,J,P$ has query cost exactly $2m$, where $m$ is the sample count for
accuracy $\tau^2/4$ and confidence parameter $1/[40(n+1)(\lceil4/\tau^2\rceil+1)]$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Candidate estimator work bound]
\lean{FABL.goldreichLevinCandidateEstimateProgram_work_le}
\label{FABL.goldreichLevinCandidateEstimateProgram_work_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.GoldreichLevinEstimateRecord, FABL.GoldreichLevinThreshold, FABL.LearningCost, FABL.LearningProgram.runWithCost, FABL.LearningProgram.runWithCost_map, FABL.fourierEstimatorSampleCount, FABL.freeFrequencyPart, FABL.goldreichLevinCallConfidence, FABL.goldreichLevinCandidateEstimateProgram, FABL.goldreichLevinWeightAccuracy, FABL.restrictedFourierWeightEstimatorCost_work_le, FABL.restrictedFourierWeightEstimatorProgram_cost_eq, FABL.scheduledRestrictedFourierWeightEstimatorProgram}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\{−1,1\}$ be any target function, let
$0<\tau\le 1$ be a rational threshold, and let $J$ and $P$ be subsets of the $n$
coordinates. Every outcome in the support of the candidate-estimation program run with
inputs $\tau,J,P$ has work cost at most $8(m+1)(n+1)$, where $m$ is the sample count for
accuracy $\tau^2/4$ and confidence parameter $1/[40(n+1)(\lceil4/\tau^2\rceil+1)]$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Stage estimate program]
\lean{FABL.goldreichLevinStageEstimateProgram}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p085-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p085-b004
}
\label{FABL.goldreichLevinStageEstimateProgram}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.GoldreichLevinEstimateRecord, FABL.GoldreichLevinThreshold, FABL.LearningProgram, FABL.LearningProgram.sequence, FABL.goldreichLevinCandidateEstimateProgram, FABL.goldreichLevinCandidates, FABL.prefixCoordinates}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\tau\in\mathbb{Q}$ satisfy $0<\tau\leq 1$, let $k$ be
a natural number with $k<n$, and let $A$ be a finite family of sets of coordinates in
$\{1,\ldots,n\}$. The stage estimate program uses membership queries to run, in
sequence, one candidate estimate program for each frequency prefix selected from $A$ by
the candidate rule at coordinate $k$; each program records the coordinate set consisting
of the first $k+1$ coordinates and that prefix, and the resulting list of records is
returned.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Keys of Stage Output Records]
\lean{FABL.goldreichLevinStageEstimateProgram_output_keys}
\label{FABL.goldreichLevinStageEstimateProgram_output_keys}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.GoldreichLevinEstimateRecord, FABL.GoldreichLevinEstimateRecord.key, FABL.GoldreichLevinThreshold, FABL.LearningCost, FABL.LearningProgram.map_output_eq_of_mem_support_sequence, FABL.LearningProgram.runWithCost, FABL.goldreichLevinCandidateEstimateProgram, FABL.goldreichLevinCandidateEstimateProgram_key, FABL.goldreichLevinCandidates, FABL.goldreichLevinStageEstimateProgram, FABL.prefixCoordinates}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f$ map the $n$-dimensional sign cube to signs,
let $0<\\tau\\le1$, and let $k<n$. For a finite family $A$ of coordinate subsets, set
$C=\\bigcup_{S\\in A}\\{S,S\\cup\\{k\\}\\}$ and $J=\\{0,\\ldots,k\\}$. In every possible
output trace of the stage run with target $f$, the sequence of pairs consisting of each
record's coordinate set and frequency prefix is exactly the list of pairs $(J,U)$ as $U$
ranges over the list of elements of $C$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Coverage of Stage Estimates]
\lean{FABL.goldreichLevinStageEstimateProgram_covers}
\label{FABL.goldreichLevinStageEstimateProgram_covers}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.GoldreichLevinEstimateRecord, FABL.GoldreichLevinEstimateRecord.Matches, FABL.GoldreichLevinEstimateRecord.key, FABL.GoldreichLevinEstimateTrace.Covers, FABL.GoldreichLevinThreshold, FABL.LearningCost, FABL.LearningProgram.runWithCost, FABL.goldreichLevinCandidates, FABL.goldreichLevinStageEstimateProgram, FABL.goldreichLevinStageEstimateProgram_output_keys, FABL.prefixCoordinates}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f$ be a function from the $n$-dimensional sign
cube to $\\{ -1,1 \\}$, let $0<\\tau\\le 1$, and let $k<n$. For any finite family $A$ of
subsets of the coordinate set, consider the stage that estimates the frequencies in
$C=\\bigcup_{S\\in A}\\{S,S\\cup\\{k\\}\\}$ using the coordinate prefix
$J=\\{0,\\ldots,k\\}$. Every possible output trace of this randomized stage contains,
for each $U\\in C$, a record whose coordinate set is $J$ and whose frequency prefix is
$U$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f$ map the $n$-dimensional sign cube to signs,
let $0<\\tau\\le1$, and let $k<n$. For a finite family $A$ of coordinate subsets, put
$C=\\bigcup_{S\\in A}\\{S,S\\cup\\{k\\}\\}$, and let $m$ be the sample count used by the
stage with accuracy parameter $\\tau^2/4$ and confidence parameter
$1/[40(n+1)(\\lceil4/\\tau^2\\rceil+1)]$. Every possible outcome of this stage uses at
most $|C|\\cdot 2m$ membership queries to the target.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f$ map the $n$-dimensional sign cube to signs,
let $0<\\tau\\le1$, and let $k<n$. For a finite family $A$ of coordinate subsets, put
$C=\\bigcup_{S\\in A}\\{S,S\\cup\\{k\\}\\}$, and let $m$ be the sample count used by the
stage with accuracy parameter $\\tau^2/4$ and confidence parameter
$1/[40(n+1)(\\lceil4/\\tau^2\\rceil+1)]$. Every possible outcome of this stage has
charged local work at most $|C|\\cdot 8(m+1)(n+1)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Stage Failure Probability Bound]
\lean{FABL.goldreichLevinStageEstimateProgram_outerFailureProbability_le}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p085-b004}
\label{FABL.goldreichLevinStageEstimateProgram_outerFailureProbability_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.GoldreichLevinEstimateRecord, FABL.GoldreichLevinEstimateRecord.IsAccurate, FABL.GoldreichLevinThreshold, FABL.LearningProgram.outerEventProbability, FABL.LearningProgram.outerEventProbability_sequence_exists_le_nsmul, FABL.goldreichLevinCallConfidence, FABL.goldreichLevinCandidateEstimateProgram, FABL.goldreichLevinCandidateEstimateProgram_outerFailureProbability_le, FABL.goldreichLevinCandidates, FABL.goldreichLevinStageEstimateProgram, FABL.prefixCoordinates}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f$ map the $n$-dimensional sign cube to signs,
let $0<\\tau\\le1$, and let $k<n$. For a finite family $A$ of coordinate subsets, put
$C=\\bigcup_{S\\in A}\\{S,S\\cup\\{k\\}\\}$. Run the stage that estimates the restricted
Fourier weight for each $U\\in C$ on the prefix $J=\\{0,\\ldots,k\\}$, using accuracy
parameter $\\tau^2/4$ and per-estimate failure parameter
$\\delta=1/[40(n+1)(\\lceil4/\\tau^2\\rceil+1)]$. The outer probability that the output
trace contains any record whose estimate differs from its corresponding restricted
Fourier weight by at least $\\tau^2/4$ is at most $|C|\\delta$.
\end{theorem}
